summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared, world-writable directory with the sticky bit set (mode 1777, owned by root:root) on the persistent XFS root filesystem. Verified with two temporary test users that both can write files but neither can remove the other's files, while each can remove their own. Performed the mandatory single-node restart via systemctl reboot, confirmed the boot ID changed (proving an actual reboot, not just a service restart), and re-verified after reboot that /srv/drop retained its 1777 root:root configuration and that the cross-user delete protection still functions. All temporary test users and files were cleaned up.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: RHEL 9.8, /srv/drop did not exist
Created test users dropuser1/dropuser2, verified dropuser1 could write, dropuser2 could also write but could NOT delete dropuser1's file (Operation not permitted)
Verified dropuser1 could delete its own file
Cleaned up test files and users
Captured baseline boot_id and directory state before restart
Triggered systemctl reboot on node1 asynchronously so the ack returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again
Confirmed boot_id changed, proving actual restart
Re-verified /srv/drop mode/ownership persisted and cross-user delete protection still works post-reboot with fresh test users
Cleaned up post-reboot verification users and files

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop created as shared writable directory with sticky bit (users cannot remove others' files)
evidence.summary: mkdir/chmod 1777/chown root:root applied; functional test showed dropuser2 could write but got 'Operation not permitted' deleting dropuser1's file, while dropuser1 could delete its own file

evidence.requirement: Node restart evidence: healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured pre-restart boot_id (6bb7e004-1e2e-46ac-bfd7-fafa248a4e76) and confirmed /srv/drop mode 1777 root:root on persistent XFS root fs

evidence.requirement: Node restart acknowledgement returns before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded systemctl reboot with 2s delay so the exec call returned successfully before the node went down

evidence.requirement: Node restart proof via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Connection timed out during reboot window (2 attempts), then node1 reachable again with new boot_id c10a9d9f-88d6-4812-8c28-5764fdf02879, differing from pre-restart value

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of /srv/drop configuration and cluster/service health
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/drop still 1777 root:root; fresh test users confirmed writable-by-all and cross-user delete still blocked (Operation not permitted); cleanup verified directory left in clean final state
